memory_leads.lead: Classification/statutory assurance spans distinct roles: owner/manager and master maintain and present the vessel; a classification society and its surveyors perform class-related assurance; flag administrations may retain or delegate statutory functions; insurers/P&I, charterers/cargo interests, financiers and port-state or other oversight actors can consume status information without sharing the same authority or claim scope.

Class status and statutory certification are separate state families. A vessel can have class-related status, class notations and class survey obligations while statutory certificates are issued or endorsed under a different authority chain; neither should be collapsed into one generic 'certified' flag.

Survey lifecycle is multi-stage: survey due or window state, booking/attendance readiness, survey attendance, findings or required follow-up, documentary completion and later closure/endorsement can occur on different clocks. Attendance itself is not proof that all obligations are closed.

Class entry and continuing class are trajectories rather than timeless labels. Initial acceptance, periodic or event-driven survey activity, ongoing conditions and later transfer/suspension/withdrawal states should be preserved as versions, while exact society procedures remain Evidence work.

Class notations or additional descriptive/technical notations are structured metadata about the basis or scope of class, not automatic proof of current operating capability, equipment performance or commercial suitability. Exact notation meanings are society- and vintage-specific.

Conditions, recommendations or other open class items form a backlog with their own issue date, scope, due state, evidence/repair requirement, survey verification and closure state. They should not be merged with the underlying physical defect or P057 maintenance backlog even when the same equipment is involved.

Damage and repair can create a distinct assurance workflow: damage occurrence/reporting, class or statutory notification, survey/assessment attendance, temporary or permanent repair state, follow-up survey and closure can diverge from the vessel's physical repair timeline and commercial availability.

Certificate lifecycle should preserve issuance/endorsement, validity window, survey linkage, extension or postponement where applicable, replacement/reissue and suspension/withdrawal states without asserting specific legal validity. One valid-looking document cannot establish the status of every statutory requirement.

Flag delegation is an authority-routing state rather than a transfer of all responsibility. A recognized/delegated organization may perform specified statutory surveys or certification functions while the flag administration remains a separate institutional actor; exact delegated scope must come from Evidence.

Class transfer is a transition chain: transfer intent/application, record and outstanding-item review, survey or information requirements, acceptance/effective transfer, prior-class closure and later continuity of records can occur on different clocks. A change of society should not erase prior open items or survey history.

Suspension, withdrawal and reinstatement/re-entry are distinct status transitions with large operational consequences, but blind Memory must not infer them from a missed survey, casualty or repair event. The trigger, effective time and consequence for a named vessel require authoritative source evidence.

Assurance status propagates into counterparties through separate acceptance decisions: insurer/P&I, lender, charterer/cargo interest, terminal/port or other authority may consider class/statutory status but can apply their own criteria. Class status therefore does not automatically determine insurance, finance, charter or port acceptance.

Class/statutory records have a point-in-time knowledge trail: survey reports, status listings, certificates, condition/recommendation records, damage/repair correspondence and transfer records may become available at different times. Later consolidated status must not be backfilled into an earlier historical decision.

P053 survey memory is refined because independent condition/cargo/on-hire surveys and classification/statutory surveys can observe overlapping physical facts but have different mandates, acceptance criteria and downstream users; surveyor attendance should therefore retain purpose/authority scope.

P057 technical-management memory is refined because a physical defect, planned-maintenance item and class/statutory condition can share an object while remaining different queues with different due/closure evidence and consequences.

P056 repair/drydock memory is refined because yard completion or successful testing does not itself close class/statutory follow-up; redelivery, survey verification, documentation and formal assurance closure can lag each other.

P044 insurance and P048 finance memory are refined because class/statutory status can be an input to coverage, covenant, valuation or acceptance decisions, but those commercial/legal effects remain separate states and cannot be inferred solely from a class record.

P053 already establishes scoped survey observation and report-known-time. P063 reuses that epistemic boundary for institutional class/statutory assurance rather than duplicating generic survey mechanics.
P057 already represents technical defects and closure backlogs. P063 adds external assurance conditions/certification states rather than creating a second physical-maintenance system.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: These are society-, flag-, vessel-, equipment- and rule-vintage-specific authoritative facts.
A named vessel's exact assurance status is a current/historical claim requiring authoritative point-in-time Evidence.
Authority scope and legal consequences are jurisdiction- and instrument-specific and cannot be inferred from blind Memory.
Organization identity, performance and current capability are source-first questions outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The classification/statutory assurance layer is populated from role/authority separation through class/statutory status, survey lifecycle, notation/open-item backlog, damage/repair follow-up, certificate lifecycle, delegation, class transfer, suspension/withdrawal and downstream counterparty use. Further recall becomes rule-, certificate-, interval-, notation-, society-, vessel-, provider- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not class, statutory, regulatory, safety, insurance, finance, chartering, port-state, seaworthiness or legal advice; no rule, survey requirement, certificate validity, notation meaning, condition, named-vessel class status, delegated authority scope, suspension/withdrawal, provider quality or legal consequence is verified.
